gloss: main enclosure of a castle; castle keep area

definitions.gloss: main enclosure of a castle; castle keep area
definitions.explanation: The innermost and most heavily fortified area of a Japanese castle, containing the main tower and lord's residence.

definitions.gloss: main target; the heart of the matter; central stronghold
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, the most important or central part of something; the real target or core issue.

examples.japanese: {本丸|ほんまる}の{石垣|いしがき}は{高|たか}くて{立派|りっぱ}だ。
examples.english: The stone walls of the main enclosure are tall and impressive.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{本丸|ほんまる}には{天守閣|てんしゅかく}がそびえていた。
examples.english: The castle tower stood towering in the main enclosure.

examples.japanese: いよいよ{本丸|ほんまる}に{切|き}り{込|こ}む。
examples.english: Now we're finally getting to the heart of the matter.

examples.japanese: {改革|かいかく}の{本丸|ほんまる}は{税制|ぜいせい}だ。
examples.english: The core of the reform is the tax system.

examples.japanese: {捜査|そうさ}はついに{本丸|ほんまる}に{迫|せま}った。
examples.english: The investigation finally closed in on the main target.

notes:
{本|ほん} (main, true) + {丸|まる} (enclosure, bailey). Originally a castle architecture term, now widely used figuratively in politics and journalism.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本丸|ほんまる}に{切|き}り{込|こ}む: get to the heart of the matter
- {本丸|ほんまる}に{迫|せま}る: close in on the main target
- {改革|かいかく}の{本丸|ほんまる}: the core of reform
- {本丸|ほんまる}{御殿|ごてん}: main enclosure palace

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {二|に}の{丸|まる}: second enclosure — the area surrounding the main enclosure
- {三|さん}の{丸|まる}: third enclosure — the outermost bailey
- {核心|かくしん}: core, crux — a more general word for the central point of an issue

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese castles were built with concentric defensive rings. The {本丸|ほんまる} was the last line of defense, containing the lord's quarters and the {天守閣|てんしゅかく} (castle tower). The figurative use — meaning the real target or the most important objective — is especially common in political reporting.
